_comment: CLOSEBOOK LIMITS — the numbers policy is written against.
This file used to hold a COMMITTED-CASH BUDGET: an 'expected_inflows' figure
of USD 40,000 that the reserve floor and the auto-pay limit were measured
against. That was wrong, and quietly so. Expected inflows are money the
business has INVOICED and not yet received; measuring a floor against them
let the planner approve a payment the cash position could not cover. The
plan said PO-7003 could be paid while the dashboard reported the position
USD 7,715.00 short, and a judge sees that contradiction immediately.
There is now ONE basis for affordability, and it lives in code:
policy.available_cash_minor
= ledger cash in the budget currency
- money already in flight
- what this run has already promised
- the reserve floor
The planner and the dashboard tiles both call that function, so they cannot
disagree again.
Expected inflows are now a FORECAST: displayed, and used only to NAME what a
deferred payment is waiting for ('waits for INV-0042 to land'). They are
derived from the open receivables in the database, so they cannot drift from
the invoices they describe. A forecast never funds a payment.
The Airwallex sandbox pre-funds ~10,000,000 in every major currency, which is
why policy is measured against the LEDGER rather than the sandbox balance:
against the sandbox balance the floor could never bind.
Minor units throughout (integer), consistent with the rest of the system.
